questions.stem: Unlike conduction and convection, thermal radiation can transfer energy through a vacuum. Why is this important for life on Earth?

options.text: It allows sound to travel from the Sun to Earth
It allows energy from the Sun to reach Earth across the vacuum of space
It keeps the atmosphere in place around the Earth
It has no practical importance

questions.explanation: Space is a vacuum with virtually no particles, so conduction and convection cannot transfer energy from the Sun to Earth. Thermal radiation (infrared electromagnetic waves) does not need particles and can travel through the vacuum of space at the speed of light. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum. This is the only way the Sun's energy reaches us.

questions.stem: Two identical metal cans are filled with hot water. Can A is painted matt black and Can B is painted shiny silver. Which cools down faster, and why?

options.text: Can B, because silver reflects heat back into the water
Both cool at the same rate because they contain the same amount of water
Can A, because dark matt surfaces are better emitters of infrared radiation
Can A, because black surfaces absorb more heat from the surroundings

questions.explanation: Dark, matt surfaces are better emitters (and absorbers) of infrared radiation than shiny, light surfaces. Can A radiates thermal energy faster, so it cools more quickly. Can B's shiny surface is a poor emitter, so it retains heat longer. Option D is about absorption, not emission. While silver does reflect radiation, the key factor here is the emission rate from the hot surface.

questions.stem: A person stands near a campfire and feels warmth on their face. Which method of heat transfer is primarily responsible?

options.text: Conduction through the air
Convection - hot air rises and hits their face
Thermal radiation (infrared waves) travelling from the fire to their skin
Conduction through the ground

questions.explanation: The warmth felt on the face when standing beside a fire is primarily due to infrared radiation travelling in straight lines from the fire. Convection carries hot air upward (not sideways toward the person). Air is a poor conductor, so conduction through air is negligible. This is why you feel warm facing the fire but not when you turn around, even at the same distance.

questions.stem: A house loses 1500 J of energy per second through its walls by radiation. The homeowner installs shiny foil insulation behind the radiators. What effect does this have?

options.text: It stops all heat loss completely
It reflects infrared radiation back into the room, reducing heat loss through the walls
It increases heat loss because foil is a good conductor
It has no effect because radiation cannot be reflected

questions.explanation: Shiny foil is an excellent reflector of infrared radiation. Placed behind radiators, it reflects the infrared radiation that would otherwise be absorbed by the wall and lost to the outside. This redirects the energy back into the room, reducing heat loss. It does not stop all heat loss (conduction through walls continues), and infrared radiation can indeed be reflected.

questions.stem: On a hot sunny day, a student touches two park benches - one painted white and one painted black. The black bench feels much hotter. Which statement best explains this?

options.text: The black bench is made of a different material
Dark surfaces are better absorbers of infrared radiation from the Sun
The white bench reflects visible light but absorbs infrared equally
The black paint generates its own heat

questions.explanation: Dark, matt surfaces are better absorbers of infrared radiation than light, shiny surfaces. The black bench absorbs more of the Sun's radiation, converting it to thermal energy, so its temperature rises more. The white bench reflects more radiation and absorbs less. Assuming the benches are the same material, the colour is the determining factor. Paint does not generate heat.
